summary: We create a prototype, in which we can identify the most suitable landing sites from a topographical perspective.
details:
Report - Astro Legion

Our group began the project by working and creating a prototype that shows the south pole of the Moon. The first thing we did was brainstorm and choose our name; in the end, we settled on Astro Legion. Afterwards, we began designing and working on the logo, aiming for it to represent the space and scientific theme of our project. In this first stage, we had to reach an agreement as a group regarding the design and name we wanted to use. This allows us to establish an identity and incorporate new ideas for its creation and development. 

One of the challenges related to space travel that NASA is analyzing and studying is the exploration of the Moon's south pole—a region of great interest due to its geography and the potential presence of frozen water. We consider this challenge highly significant, as it would serve as a precursor to future missions to Mars. Consequently, exploring the area and confirming the existence of resources such as water would be essential for human settlement on the Moon. 

To address this issue, Astro Legion proposed a web prototype that allows for the specific analysis of the most suitable lunar landing sites for future missions. The website is designed for a general audience—including students, researchers, and mission planners—as it is user-friendly, featuring a straightforward section for beginners and an advanced section for professionals. 

It is a bilingual prototype, as it offers the option to switch the entire interface language between English and Spanish.

It allows you to select an exact date (year, month, and day) to obtain data in advance. In "advanced" mode, Astro Legion provides the following information: the coordinates of points selected on the chart, solar illumination, communication with Earth, the elevation of the Sun and Earth, and terrain details. In "simple" mode, it provides: coordinates, solar illumination, and communication with Earth. 

Additionally, the bottom navigation bar on our website provides more detailed information regarding the map, the two selected points, and the Moon. In the section dedicated to these points, you will find a 30-day (one-month) calendar showing solar illumination and communication status with Earth; a green indicator signifies optimal conditions, while pink indicates suboptimal conditions. The Moon section offers more specific lunar data, such as the current lunar phase and the dates of upcoming phases. It also displays the positions of the Sun and Earth.

In the main "Map" section, you can view an interactive image of the lunar South Pole. We used NASA’s "Moon Trek" resource to obtain a detailed, realistic image, and layered it with additional data—such as a mosaic, shaded relief, and LOLA (Lunar Orbiter Laser Altimeter) data. 

We initially designed the interface on paper, iterating through several versions to refine the layout and incorporate various tools. Next, we used an AI tool called "Claude" to generate the necessary code in JavaScript (JS). We then pasted this code into the source-code editor "Visual Studio Code," where we integrated the image downloaded from "Moon Trek" (in JPG format) to create an interactive experience.

We can conclude that the use of Astro Legion across various levels of expertise facilitates an understanding of the significance of lunar missions, while simultaneously helping professionals in this field of exploration to refine their preparations—enabling them to anticipate as much as possible before embarking on new missions.

We thank you for the opportunity to bring these events to cities that are not as large or well-known—such as San Luis, Argentina—thereby giving us young people the chance to put our skills into practice and to develop our intellect and love for astronomy. Thank you for the food, entertainment, and support we received, and for allowing minors to participate in this.

- Astro Legion
